description: Stereo distortion modelled on a guitar pedal's diode clipper, with a filter that sweeps from dark to bright and a dry/wet mix

params.text: Runs the signal through the distortion when on; with it off the module is bypassed, and the switch crossfades between the two rather than stepping
Sweeps a filter from lowpass through mid-cut to highpass, taking the sound from darker to brighter; the readout runs 0 to 11
Sets the gain into the diode clipper, so turning it up squares the signal off harder; the clipping is soft rather than hard, despite the panel printing DIST
Sets how much of the distorted signal is in the output against the dry input, 0 to 100% wet

inputs.text: Adds to the TONE knob, where 10V covers the whole of that knob's travel
Adds to the DIST knob, where 10V covers the whole of that knob's travel
Adds to the MIX knob, where 10V covers the whole of that knob's travel
Adds to the LEVEL knob, where 10V covers the whole of that knob's travel
The left audio input into the distortion
The right audio input into the distortion

outputs.text: The left output, carrying the dry signal and the distortion in the proportion set by MIX
The right output, carrying the dry signal and the distortion in the proportion set by MIX

notes: the two channels are separate circuits and neither input is normalled to the other, so with nothing patched into IN II the OUT II jack stays at 0V
the circuit is modelled around a signal of ±1, and the module divides each input by 5 and multiplies each output by 5 to suit it, so ±5V is the level it expects
